title: Blackcurrant and strawberry compote with yoghurt

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Fruit, honey, oats, seeds, Greek yoghurt, lemon and mint are all ordinary home kitchen and garden foods.

supermarket.reason: Fresh blackcurrants can be patchy in early June, but the step gives raspberries as a fallback and everything else is an everyday supermarket item.

basic_kitchen.reason: Only a small pan and a frying pan are needed, and simmering fruit and dry-toasting oats are beginner techniques.

works.reason: 150g blackcurrants and 300g strawberries over 500g yoghurt with toasted oats and seeds makes a sensible breakfast for four, and the strawberries soften the tartness of the currants.

honest_times.reason: Ten minutes covers stripping the currants, halving the strawberries and assembling, and the 4, 1 and 3 to 4 minute stages roughly match the 8 minutes of cooking.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning is used, the names match their ids, and the raspberry substitute is on the June fresh list.

seasonal_feel.reason: A warm fruit compote with yoghurt suits a June morning, and the blackcurrants give the compote its sharp character even though they are outweighed by the strawberries.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear British English with no restaurant language or preaching.

hearty_healthy.reason: Greek yoghurt, fruit, oats and pumpkin seeds make a filling breakfast with only a spoon of honey.
